correctness.rationale: PASS. For the Wolfram Rule-54 map specified by its eight three-bit input neighborhoods, four input pair states form a labelled de Bruijn graph. A periodic output word w^Z has any biinfinite preimage iff its Boolean relation R(w) contains a directed cycle; it has an n-periodic predecessor for |w|=n iff R(w) has a diagonal loop. Exhaustive closure of all products of two 4x4 Boolean adjacency generators has exactly 109 matrices, 77 with a loop, 31 acyclic, one cyclic but loopless. My independent monoid implementation verified that the exceptional matrix is R_1, that its only entering right-transition is I --1--> R_1, and there are no transitions into I; thus the only word with a cyclic relation but no loop is length-one '1'. Consequently F(P_n)=Y∩P_n for every n>=2. The constant output 1^Z is in Y via alternating predecessor but neither constant input maps to it, giving the unique n=1 exception. When output has least period n, a P_n predecessor must also have least period n by shift commutation. Ring tests ≤12 are separate corroboration, not all-n proof. The 109-state finite closure is genuinely exhaustive, not mere length-cutoff testing.
